submitted.rationale: Of the 3 measured compositions, the Fe-richest one (Fe0.81Sb0.19, likely Sb-doped hematite with some FeSbO4) was the only one with a positive EQE at 2.1 eV: 0.0057%. The FeSbO4 composition (idx 12) and the Sb-rich composition (idx 20) both came out at about zero or slightly negative.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE about -0.0003%. FeSbO4 is stable and its predicted gap (2.08 eV) is right at the photon energy, but it showed no photoresponse.
Measured EQE about -0.0003%. The Sb-rich trirutile/Sb-oxide region is inactive.
Not measured because the budget ran out. The GP mean there is below idx 0, and the trend suggests EQE rises with Fe content.

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile FeSbO4 is on the MACE hull (0.002 eV/atom) and MEGNet HSE gap 2.08 eV matches the 2.1 eV illumination, so near-stoichiometric Fe0.51Sb0.49 (idx 12) should be single-phase FeSbO4 and absorb.

Weak support. MEGNet gaps for hematite vary a lot between fidelities (HSE 2.77, SCAN 0.81), which puts the real ~2.1 eV gap in range for 2.1 eV light. FeSbO4 at idx 12 gave about zero EQE. The Fe-rich end (Sb-doped hematite with some FeSbO4) is the best-motivated remaining region.

Uninformative to weak support. The Sb-rich phases (FeSb2O4 HSE 2.38 eV, FeSb2O6 1.28 eV) have gaps on either side of 2.1 eV, so that side may absorb. Fe-rich idx 0 is already secured (EQE 0.0057), and interpolating toward idx 12 (about zero) probably won't beat it. The unexplored Sb-rich trirutile region gives the most upside for the last measurement.
